### EP-01

**No non-essential cookies before consent** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Guidelines 2/2023 on Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) of ePrivacy Directive, version 2.0](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-22023-technical-scope-art-53-eprivacy-directive_en) — EU, non-binding guidelines; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CJEU: Judgment of 1 October 2019, Planet49, C-673/17, ECLI:EU:C:2019:801](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62017CJ0673) — EU, binding case law; verified 2026-10-16
  - [Article 29 Working Party: Opinion 04/2012 on Cookie Consent Exemption (WP 194)](https://ec.europa.eu/justice/article-29/documentation/opinion-recommendation/files/2012/wp194_en.pdf) — EU, non-binding opinion; verified 2026-10-16
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §8, paras 26-30 (cookies inaccurately classified as essential) — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: No cookie classified as analytics, marketing or otherwise requiring consent was stored while the page was observed ({window} after loading, with no interaction). {exempt_summary}
- Wording when *fail*: {count} cookie(s) classified as requiring consent were stored before any interaction with the page: {items}. Art. 5(3) requires prior consent for storing information on the visitor's device unless it is strictly necessary for a service the visitor requested.
- Wording when *manual review*: No cookie known to require consent was found, but {count} cookie(s) stored before any interaction could not be confirmed as exempt: {items}. Their purpose has to be checked before drawing a conclusion.
- Hint: Load analytics and advertising tags only after the visitor accepts them (for example through the consent platform's blocking mode or consent mode), and document the purpose of each remaining cookie.

### EP-02

**No third-party tracking requests before consent** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Guidelines 2/2023 on Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) of ePrivacy Directive, version 2.0](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-22023-technical-scope-art-53-eprivacy-directive_en), §3.1 (URL and pixel tracking) — EU, non-binding guidelines; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: No request to a known analytics or advertising service, and no unclassified beacon-like request, was observed before any interaction. {other_summary}
- Wording when *fail*: {count} known tracking service(s) were contacted before any interaction with the page: {items}. The EDPB considers that sending information from the device through tracking pixels and URLs falls within Art. 5(3) and requires prior consent unless an exemption applies.
- Wording when *manual review*: No known tracking service was contacted, but {count} third-party site(s) received requests before any interaction that may be tracking: {items}. Whether consent was required depends on what they collect.
- Hint: Defer third-party pixels, beacons and tags until consent is given, or document why each remaining third-party request is strictly necessary.

### EP-03

**No known tracker identifiers in Web Storage before consent** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Guidelines 2/2023 on Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) of ePrivacy Directive, version 2.0](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-22023-technical-scope-art-53-eprivacy-directive_en) — EU, non-binding guidelines; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: No localStorage or sessionStorage key associated with analytics or advertising was written before any interaction. {other_summary}
- Wording when *fail*: {count} Web Storage key(s) associated with analytics or advertising were written before any interaction: {items}. Art. 5(3) applies to any storage on the device, not only to cookies.
- Wording when *manual review*: {count} Web Storage key(s) written before any interaction look like identifiers or come from third parties and could not be classified: {items}. Their purpose has to be checked.
- Hint: Make scripts that write identifiers to localStorage or sessionStorage wait for consent, like cookie-setting scripts.

### EP-04

**Consent mechanism present when trackers are used** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj); [GDPR, Art. 4(11) and Art. 7](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §3, para 7 — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: A consent interface was detected on the page ({banner}).
- Wording when *fail*: Trackers requiring consent were observed ({trackers}), but no consent interface was detected on the first screen. Consent under Art. 5(3) has to be obtained before such trackers are used.
- Wording when *manual review*: {detail}
- Wording when *not applicable*: No tracker requiring consent was observed and no consent interface was detected. A consent banner is only needed when non-exempt trackers are used, so its absence is not an issue in itself. Trackers that only load after an interaction would not have been observed.
- Hint: Show a consent interface before any non-exempt tracker is used, or remove the trackers.

### EP-05

**Reject option on the first layer of the banner** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj); [GDPR, Art. 4(11) and Art. 7](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §3, paras 6-8 (Type A: no reject button on the first layer) — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CNIL: Délibération n° 2020-092 du 17 septembre 2020 portant adoption d'une recommandation (cookies et autres traceurs), consolidated version as amended by délibération n° 2025-131 du 18 décembre 2025](https://cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2026-01/recommandation_cookies_consolidee.pdf), §2.3 (refusal as easy as consent, same screen) — FR, non-binding recommendation; verified 2026-10-16
  - [Conseil d'État (FR): CE, 19 juin 2026, n° 501417, association Pour un RGPD respecté et autres (CNIL recommendation, "continuer sans accepter")](https://www.conseil-etat.fr/fr/arianeweb/CE/decision/2026-06-19/501417) — FR, binding case law; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: The first layer of the consent interface offers a refusal option ({reject}) alongside acceptance ({accept}).
- Wording when *fail*: The first layer of the consent interface offers acceptance ({accept}) but no refusal option was found; other controls: {others}. The CNIL strongly recommends that refusing be possible on the same screen and as easily as accepting, and most authorities in the EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce considered a banner with no refusal option on any layer to be an infringement.
- Wording when *manual review*: {detail}
- Wording when *not applicable*: {detail}
- Hint: Add a "Tout refuser" / "Reject all" button (or a clearly labelled "Continuer sans accepter" link) to the first layer, next to the accept button.

### EP-06

**Reject comparable in prominence to accept** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj); [GDPR, Art. 4(11) and Art. 7(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §6, paras 15-19 (deceptive button colours and contrast) — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CNIL: Délibération n° 2020-092 du 17 septembre 2020 portant adoption d'une recommandation (cookies et autres traceurs), consolidated version as amended by délibération n° 2025-131 du 18 décembre 2025](https://cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2026-01/recommandation_cookies_consolidee.pdf), §2.3 — FR, non-binding recommendation; verified 2026-10-16
  - CNIL: Délibérations SAN-2021-023 (Google LLC and Google Ireland Limited) and SAN-2021-024 (Facebook Ireland Limited) of 31 December 2021 — FR, non-binding decision; **not yet verified**

### EP-07

**Refusal honoured (no trackers after reject)** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj)

### EP-08

**Persistent way to withdraw or change consent** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [GDPR, Art. 7(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §9, paras 31-32 (no withdraw icon) — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CNIL: Délibération n° 2020-092 du 17 septembre 2020 portant adoption d'une recommandation (cookies et autres traceurs), consolidated version as amended by délibération n° 2025-131 du 18 décembre 2025](https://cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2026-01/recommandation_cookies_consolidee.pdf), §3 — FR, non-binding recommendation; verified 2026-10-16

### EP-09

**Audience-measurement cookie lifetime within 13 months** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj); [GDPR, Art. 5(1)(e)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [CNIL: Délibération n° 2020-092 du 17 septembre 2020 portant adoption d'une recommandation (cookies et autres traceurs), consolidated version as amended by délibération n° 2025-131 du 18 décembre 2025](https://cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2026-01/recommandation_cookies_consolidee.pdf), §5 (audience-measurement trackers: lifetime such as thirteen months) — FR, non-binding recommendation; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CNIL: Cookies : solutions pour les outils de mesure d'audience](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/cookies-et-autres-traceurs/regles/cookies-solutions-pour-les-outils-de-mesure-daudience) — FR, non-binding guidance; verified 2026-10-16
  - [CNIL: Délibération n° 2020-091 du 17 septembre 2020 portant adoption de lignes directrices relatives à l'application de l'article 82 de la loi du 6 janvier 1978 modifiée (cookies et autres traceurs)](https://www.cnil.fr/sites/cnil/files/atoms/files/lignes_directrices_de_la_cnil_sur_les_cookies_et_autres_traceurs.pdf), Art. 5 (audience measurement) — FR, non-binding guidelines; verified 2026-10-16
- Wording when *pass*: The analytics cookie(s) stored before consent have a lifetime of 13 months or less: {items}.
- Wording when *fail*: {count} analytics cookie(s) stored before consent have a lifetime above 13 months: {items}. A site relying on the CNIL audience-measurement exemption is expected to limit tracker lifetime, for example to thirteen months (French guidance). {cap_note}
- Wording when *not applicable*: No analytics cookie was stored before consent, so no audience-measurement lifetime applies to this observation.
- Hint: Configure the analytics tool to cap its cookie lifetime at 13 months and not to extend it on each visit.

### EP-10

**No cookie wall (access conditioned on acceptance)** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj); [GDPR, Art. 7(4)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [Conseil d'État (FR): CE, 19 juin 2020, n° 434684, Association des agences-conseils en communication et autres (annulment of the general cookie-wall ban in CNIL deliberation 2019-093)](https://www.conseil-etat.fr/fr/arianeweb/CE/decision/2020-06-19/434684) — FR, binding case law; verified 2026-10-16
- What to review: Check whether refusing trackers blocks or degrades access to the content. Positions differ between member states (in France, case by case since the Conseil d'État decision of 19 June 2020; other authorities are stricter), so this needs a jurisdiction-specific assessment.

### EP-11

**Granular purposes, no pre-ticked purposes in the second layer** · v1.0.0

- Legal basis: [GDPR, Art. 4(11) and Recital 32](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
- Interpretation:
  - [CJEU: Judgment of 1 October 2019, Planet49, C-673/17, ECLI:EU:C:2019:801](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62017CJ0673) — EU, binding case law; verified 2026-10-16
  - [EDPB: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/2023-01/edpb_20230118_report_cookie_banner_taskforce_en.pdf), §4, paras 9-10 (pre-ticked boxes) — EU, non-binding report; verified 2026-10-16
- What to review: Open the banner's settings layer and check that each purpose can be accepted or refused separately and that no purpose is enabled by default.

## Always requires manual review (never scored)

| ID | Topic | Provision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-01 | Validity of each legal basis, including legitimate-interest balancing | GDPR Art. 6(1), in particular Art. 6(1)(f) | Depends on purposes and internal assessments not visible on the website. |
| M-02 | Accuracy of the privacy notice compared with actual processing | GDPR Art. 5(1)(a), Art. 13 | Requires knowledge of the organisation's real processing activities. |
| M-03 | Whether a data protection officer is mandatory | GDPR Art. 37 | Depends on the organisation's core activities and scale. |
| M-04 | Records of processing activities | GDPR Art. 30 | Internal document. |
| M-05 | Data protection impact assessments | GDPR Art. 35 | Internal document. |
| M-06 | Processor contracts | GDPR Art. 28 | Contracts with service providers are not public. |
| M-07 | Security of processing | GDPR Art. 32 | HTTPS is a visible signal only; security measures are mostly internal. |
| M-08 | Retention actually applied | GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) | Stated retention can be read; applied retention cannot be observed. |
| M-09 | Handling of data subject requests | GDPR Arts. 12, 15-22 | Requires exercising the rights and observing the response. |
| M-10 | Validity of the international transfer mechanism | GDPR Chapter V (Arts. 44-49) | Adequacy, DPF certification or SCCs are not observable from requests. |
| M-11 | Joint controllership for embedded third-party content | GDPR Art. 26; CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID | Depends on arrangements between the site and the third party. |
| M-12 | Children's consent for information society services | GDPR Art. 8 | Depends on the audience and on age-verification practices. |

## Disclaimer printed on every report

Automated technical observation of one page load from one vantage point. It is not a legal assessment and not legal advice. "No issue detected" means the scanner did not observe an issue, not that the site meets its legal obligations.
